::: {.bnr-manual-flag .bnr-manual-flag--technical}
Technical Manual
:::

## What this page does

The one-off report workflow packages a completed analyst-produced PDF, creates its public landing page, records approval and publishes the exact approved files. A report may also include one associated public dataset package containing CSV, labelled Stata DTA and TXT metadata files.

The workflow does not run, standardise or verify the analysis method. Complete and retain the analysis code, sources, reproducibility record and review evidence in approved private locations before starting.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Procedure at a glance"}
1. Complete the analysis, PDF and disclosure review.
2. Run Step 1 and review the three-file report package or five-file report-and-dataset package.
3. Run Step 2 to approve the unchanged manifested package.
4. Run Step 3 to publish the approved report.
5. Render and review the landing page, PDF and automatic report listings.
:::

## Before you start

- Choose a stable study ID containing lowercase letters, numbers and underscores and beginning with a letter—for example, `case_fatality_2025`.
- Choose a positive whole-number report version and an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` report date.
- Prepare a non-empty final PDF in an approved private location.
- If the report has an associated public dataset, prepare all three public inputs: CSV, labelled DTA and TXT metadata. Suppression must already have been applied and explained in those files.
- Prepare the public title and short description. Neither may contain a double quotation mark.
- Complete and record the report’s analytical and disclosure review. The optional screening utility below supports review but does not replace it.

In the file patterns below, `STUDY_ID` is the chosen study ID, `REVIEW_ID` is the optional screen ID and `N` is the report version.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Input files"}

| File | What the workflow uses or checks |
|---|---|
| Finished private report PDF | Step 1 checks that it exists and is non-empty, then copies it unchanged into the private proposed package. |
| Optional associated CSV, DTA and TXT metadata | Supply all three or none. Step 1 checks that each exists and is non-empty, then creates one folder-aware ZIP containing `data/` and `metadata/` folders. |
| Optional private Stata count dataset | The disclosure-screen utility requires `output_id`, `cell_id` and numeric `cell_count`. It is not read by Steps 1–3. |

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Code files"}

| File | How it is used |
|---|---|
| `scripts/stata/reporting/bnr_report_disclosure_screen.do` | Optional utility that flags counts and structural issues for human disclosure review. |
| `scripts/stata/reporting/bnr_report_oneoff_s1_prepare.do` | Step 1 controller; copies the PDF, optionally creates the dataset ZIP and catalogue record, and creates the landing page and report description. |
| `scripts/stata/reporting/bnr_report_oneoff_s2_approve.do` | Step 2 approval controller. |
| `scripts/stata/reporting/bnr_report_approve_candidate.do` | Shared helper that verifies the complete reviewed payload and creates approval evidence. |
| `scripts/stata/reporting/bnr_report_oneoff_s3_publish.do` | Step 3 publication controller. |
| `scripts/stata/reporting/bnr_report_publish_candidate.do` | Shared helper that verifies and publishes the complete approved payload. |
| `scripts/stata/dialogs/bnr_report_disclosure_screen.dlg` | Stata dialog for the optional disclosure screen. |
| `scripts/stata/dialogs/bnr_report_oneoff_s1_prepare.dlg` | Step 1 Stata dialog. |
| `scripts/stata/dialogs/bnr_report_oneoff_s2_approve.dlg` | Step 2 Stata dialog. |
| `scripts/stata/dialogs/bnr_report_oneoff_s3_publish.dlg` | Step 3 Stata dialog. |
| `scripts/stata/menu/bnr_menu.do` | Adds the screening utility and three one-off-report steps to the BNR Stata menu. |

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Output files"}

The optional screen writes private files under `$BNR_STAGING/report_reviews/disclosure/REVIEW_ID/`.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `disclosure_screen.csv` | Row-level screening results and reasons for human review. |
| `screen_summary.yml` | Generated summary of the input file and screening counts. |
| `$BNR_PRIVATE_LOGS/bnr_report_disclosure_screen_REVIEW_ID.log` | Private screening log. |

Step 1 always creates three private proposed report files under `$BNR_STAGING/reports/cvd/studies/bnr_cvd_oneoff_STUDY_ID_vN/candidate/`.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `bnr_cvd_oneoff_STUDY_ID_vN.pdf` | Unchanged private copy of the finished PDF. **Open this first.** |
| `index.qmd` | Generated proposed public landing page. |
| `report.yml` | Generated report identity, study ID, version, date, public filename and PDF checksum—a value used to detect a changed file. |

When all three associated-data inputs are supplied, Step 1 also creates:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `bnr_cvd_oneoff_STUDY_ID_data.zip` | Folder-aware ZIP containing the public CSV and DTA under `data/` and the TXT metadata under `metadata/`. |
| `bnr_cvd_oneoff_STUDY_ID_data.yml` | Catalogue record used to add the ZIP to the central downloads page. |

Step 2 copies the three or five unchanged files into `public_ready/` and adds:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `public_manifest.csv` | Private generated list of the exact three or five files Step 3 may publish, with file sizes and checksums. |
| `approval.yml` | Private approval record, written last. Approval does not mean publication. |

`public_ready` is the private folder holding the files authorised for Step 3. It is not a public location.

Step 3 publishes stable public filenames:

| File | Published location |
|---|---|
| `bnr_cvd_oneoff_STUDY_ID.pdf` | `$BNR_PUBLIC/reports/cvd/studies/STUDY_ID/` and `site/downloads/files/reports/cvd/studies/STUDY_ID/`. |
| `index.qmd` | Official public study folder and `site/surveillance/cvd/reports/studies/STUDY_ID/`. |
| `report.yml` | Official public study folder and website-download folder. |
| Associated dataset ZIP | Official public study folder and `site/downloads/files/reports/cvd/studies/STUDY_ID/`. |
| Dataset catalogue YML | `catalogue/` below the corresponding authoritative and website-download study folders. |

Private Step 1–3 logs are written under `$BNR_PRIVATE_LOGS/` with the report ID in each filename.

:::

## Optional: screen structured counts

This utility is an early-warning screen, not disclosure control. It flags integer counts from 0 to 5, missing or negative values, non-integer counts and duplicate cell IDs for human review. A flagged zero is not automatically suppressed under the BNR publication rule; positive counts from 1 to 5 require protection.

1. In Stata, choose **User > BNR > Report utilities > Screen report counts for disclosure review**.
2. Select the private Stata dataset and enter a stable review ID. Leave replacement unticked for the first screen and select **Screen counts**.
3. Alternatively, enter the complete routine command in the **Stata command window**:

   ```stata
   do "$BNR_STATA/reporting/bnr_report_disclosure_screen.do" ///
       "$BNR_STAGING/report_inputs/report_counts.dta" case_fatality_2025
   ```

4. To rebuild the same private screen deliberately, enter the complete replacement command:

   ```stata
   do "$BNR_STATA/reporting/bnr_report_disclosure_screen.do" ///
       "$BNR_STAGING/report_inputs/report_counts.dta" case_fatality_2025 replace
   ```

5. In `REPORT DISCLOSURE SCREEN: OPERATIONAL RUN SUMMARY`, confirm `Run status: Screening completed`.
6. Review every row marked `REVIEW` in `disclosure_screen.csv`, then complete the whole-report disclosure assessment. The screen does not apply additional protection, alter the PDF, approve the report or publish anything.

## Step 1: prepare and review the proposed report

1. In Stata, choose **User > BNR > One-off CVD report publication > Step 1: Prepare one-off report candidate**.
2. Enter the study ID, report version, report date, finished PDF path, public title and description. If applicable, also enter all three associated-data paths. Leave replacement unticked for the first build and select **Prepare candidate**.
3. Alternatively, enter the complete routine command in the **Stata command window**:

   ```stata
   do "$BNR_STATA/reporting/bnr_report_oneoff_s1_prepare.do" ///
       case_fatality_2025 1 "C:\path\report.pdf" ///
       "Public report title" "Public description" 2026-09-17
   ```

   For a report with an associated dataset, the empty quoted argument preserves the optional replacement position:

   ```stata
   do "$BNR_STATA/reporting/bnr_report_oneoff_s1_prepare.do" ///
       case_fatality_2025 1 "C:\path\report.pdf" ///
       "Public report title" "Public description" 2026-09-17 "" ///
       "C:\path\case_fatality_metrics.csv" ///
       "C:\path\case_fatality_metrics.dta" ///
       "C:\path\case_fatality_metadata.txt"
   ```

4. To rebuild the same unapproved version deliberately, enter the complete replacement command:

   ```stata
   do "$BNR_STATA/reporting/bnr_report_oneoff_s1_prepare.do" ///
       case_fatality_2025 1 "C:\path\report.pdf" ///
       "Public report title" "Public description" 2026-09-17 replace
   ```

5. In `ONE-OFF CVD REPORT STEP 1: OPERATIONAL RUN SUMMARY`, confirm `Run status: Candidate prepared` and check the report ID and private folder.
6. Open the copied PDF first and confirm it is the reviewed finished report and is disclosure-safe.
7. Review every table, chart, explanatory statement and public download together to confirm that no protected value is shown or can be calculated.
8. Preview `index.qmd` and check the study ID, title, description, date, version, image, alternative text, PDF link and—when present—dataset link.
9. Open `report.yml` and confirm the report identity and PDF information. For an associated dataset, also inspect the ZIP contents and catalogue YML.

If the version has already been approved, create and review a higher version instead of rebuilding it.

## Step 2: approve the reviewed package

1. In Stata, choose **User > BNR > One-off CVD report publication > Step 2: Approve one-off report candidate**.
2. Enter the study ID, version, approver’s full name and authorised role.
3. Confirm that the complete proposed package was reviewed, disclosure review was completed and the exact files are ready for publication.
4. Select **Approve candidate**.
5. Alternatively, enter the complete command in the **Stata command window**:

   ```stata
   do "$BNR_STATA/reporting/bnr_report_oneoff_s2_approve.do" ///
       case_fatality_2025 1 "Full Name" "BNR Analyst" ///
       candidate disclosure ready
   ```

6. In `ONE-OFF CVD REPORT STEP 2: OPERATIONAL RUN SUMMARY`, confirm `Run status: Candidate approved`.
7. Confirm `public_manifest.csv` lists exactly three files for a PDF-only report or five files for a report with an associated dataset. Confirm `approval.yml` identifies the correct approver, role, study and version.

Only an authorised **BNR Lead** or **BNR Analyst** may approve. Step 2 has no `replace` option.

## Step 3: publish the approved report

1. In Stata, choose **User > BNR > One-off CVD report publication > Step 3: Publish approved one-off report**.
2. Enter the approved study ID and version. Leave replacement unticked for first publication and select **Publish one-off report**.
3. Alternatively, enter the complete routine command in the **Stata command window**:

   ```stata
   do "$BNR_STATA/reporting/bnr_report_oneoff_s3_publish.do" case_fatality_2025 1
   ```

4. For controlled republication of an existing approved version, enter the complete replacement command:

   ```stata
   do "$BNR_STATA/reporting/bnr_report_oneoff_s3_publish.do" case_fatality_2025 1 replace
   ```

5. In `ONE-OFF CVD REPORT STEP 3: OPERATIONAL RUN SUMMARY`, confirm `Run status: Published successfully` and check the public and website locations.
6. Confirm every official public file matches the approved manifest. When present, open the dataset ZIP and confirm the landing-page download works.
7. Run `python site/scripts/build_download_catalogue.py`, then complete a full local Quarto render. Open the PDF and landing page and check both automatic report listings and the central downloads page.
8. Review all Git changes before following the normal development-branch deployment route.

Use a higher approved version for a correction. Same-version `replace` is reserved for controlled recovery and the publisher refuses a downgrade.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="If a one-off-report step does not complete"}

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| The proposed PDF does not match the supplied PDF | Stop and inspect both files. Recreate the Step 1 package; do not replace one generated file manually. |
| A reviewed file changed before approval | Rerun Step 1 and repeat the complete review. |
| Existing public output blocks Step 3 | Confirm the intended approved version. Use a higher version for a correction or `replace` only for controlled same-version recovery. |

For other problems, see [Troubleshoot the workflow](../../maintenance/troubleshooting.qmd).

:::
